required_stages.description: Compute K' = smallest power of two >= k and choose a block width B >= 2*K' inside run().

A launch that cuts the current vector into contiguous blocks of width B padded with -inf, selects each block's K' largest values in descending order with an exact in-block primitive (block top-k builtin, bitonic sort + prefix, or equivalent) and writes them as rows of a fresh (nb, K') fp32 buffer.
Repeat the block level on the flattened candidate buffer until a single block remains; each level is its own launch and depends on the previous level's buffer.
Return the first k entries of the final single-block row as a 1-D (k,) fp32 tensor that does not alias the input.

forbidden_substitutions.message: The whole selection is performed by a PyTorch top-k / sort routine.
A tensor-method sort on the host replaces the in-kernel hierarchy.
Host-side PyTorch reduction / histogram / threshold operations indicate a different selection family or host-side selection.
Data moved to the host or selected in Python.
Radix-select / histogram-threshold selection is a different algorithm family from the hierarchical block tournament.
Returning a view of the input or mutating it violates the aliasing / no-mutation rules.
Ascending / smallest selection; the output must be the k largest in descending order.

required_evidence.message: No in-block selection / sort primitive found.
No -inf padding evidence for partial blocks.
No evidence of the per-block candidate width K' = next power of two >= k.
No level loop found; the hierarchy must repeat until one block remains.
No final slice to exactly k values found.

outputs.aliasing: a 1-D fp32 (k,) tensor; may be a slice/view of a candidate buffer allocated inside run() (both references return out[0, :k] of the final (1, K') buffer); must never be a view of or share storage with input

timing_boundary.notes: Everything inside run() is timed: K' and block-width arithmetic, every per-level candidate buffer allocation, every level launch and the final slice. No cached state across calls, no host-side sort or copy of the input, no prepacking. The per-level candidate buffers are part of the canonical algorithm, not preprocessing.
